To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the contribution of German universal banks to the development of German industry was limited; (ii) the distinctive features of the relationships between universal banks and German industry applied to industrial joint-stock firms only; and (iii) even in the case of industrial joint-stock companies the relationship between banks and industry was not as close as has been suggested by some historians.

(a) the contribution of universal banks (and of all banks) to German industrialization was relatively small; and (b) the relationship between universal banking and the German industrial economy was not the same as that between the British merchant banks and the British industrial economy, and the conventional view of the relationship between German universal banks and industrial joint-stock companies is seriously flawed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of universal banking in the development of Germany as an industrial economy.
three main questions: What was the role of banks in German industrial development?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
universal banks were a minor influence on the German economy before 1914, and that their influence on the German industrial economy was limited.
universal banks did not play a major role in German industrialization.
, although the relationship between universal bankers and industrialists was important, it was not crucial to the development of German industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
universal banks played a significant role in the financing of German industrialization, but that their importance has been exaggerated.

the role of the German universal banks in the financing of industrial joint-stock companies was not a major factor in the process of industrialization, and their role in the financing of the German economy was much less significant than has been suggested.
universal banks were important in German industrialization, but not as important as is often suggested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
universal banks were not the main source of industrial finance in Germany.
, in the case of Germany at least, the conventional view of the role of universal banking in industrialization is not well supported by the evidence.
universal banks did not have the same role in German industrialization as they did in the Japanese case.
